questions.question: What is HTML?
questions.answer: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard markup language for creating web pages. It provides the structure and content of web pages.

questions.question: What is the difference between HTML and HTML5?
questions.answer: HTML5 is the latest version of HTML with new features like semantic elements, audio/video support, canvas, and improved APIs.

questions.question: What is a semantic HTML element?
questions.answer: Semantic HTML elements have meaning beyond their appearance. Examples include <header>, <nav>, <article>, <section>, and <footer>.

questions.question: What are HTML form input types?
questions.answer: HTML input types include text, email, password, number, checkbox, radio, file, date, time, and more. Each type provides specific validation and user interface.

questions.question: What is the alt attribute in images?
questions.answer: The alt attribute provides alternative text for images. It's displayed if the image fails to load and helps screen readers describe images to visually impaired users.

questions.question: What is the meta viewport tag?
questions.answer: The meta viewport tag controls layout on mobile browsers. It tells the browser to render the page at the device's width and set appropriate zoom levels.

questions.question: What is the difference between <article> and <section>?
questions.answer: <article> represents independent, self-contained content. <section> groups related content together. <article> can contain multiple <section>s.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the <head> tag?
questions.answer: The <head> tag contains metadata about the document, including title, meta tags, links to stylesheets, and scripts. It's not displayed on the page.

questions.question: What is the difference between <label> and placeholder?
questions.answer: <label> is a semantic element that associates text with form inputs for accessibility. Placeholder is temporary text inside the input that disappears when typing.

questions.question: What is ARIA in HTML?
questions.answer: ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) provides attributes to improve accessibility. It helps screen readers understand dynamic content and interactive elements.

questions.question: What is the <nav> element?
questions.answer: The <nav> element represents a section of navigation links. It's used for main navigation menus and link groups.

questions.question: What is the <header> element?
questions.answer: The <header> element represents introductory content or a group of navigational links. It typically contains the site logo and main navigation.

questions.question: What is the <footer> element?
questions.answer: The <footer> element represents footer content of a section or page. It typically contains copyright information and links.

questions.question: What is the <main> element?
questions.answer: The <main> element represents the main content of a page. There should be only one <main> element per page.

questions.question: What is the <aside> element?
questions.answer: The <aside> element represents content aside from the main content. It's typically used for sidebars and related information.

questions.question: What is the <figure> element?
questions.answer: The <figure> element represents self-contained illustrations, diagrams, or code examples. It's often used with <figcaption>.

questions.question: What is the <figcaption> element?
questions.answer: The <figcaption> element provides a caption for a <figure> element. It helps describe the figure's content.

questions.question: What is the <time> element?
questions.answer: The <time> element represents a specific time or date. It helps machines understand temporal information.

questions.question: What is the <mark> element?
questions.answer: The <mark> element highlights text for reference or relevance. It's typically displayed with a yellow background.

questions.question: What is the <strong> element?
questions.answer: The <strong> element indicates strong importance. It's typically displayed in bold and conveys semantic importance.

questions.question: What is the <em> element?
questions.answer: The <em> element indicates emphasis. It's typically displayed in italics and conveys semantic emphasis.

questions.question: What is the <small> element?
questions.answer: The <small> element represents small text like copyright or legal information. It's typically displayed in smaller font.

questions.question: What is the <code> element?
questions.answer: The <code> element represents computer code. It's typically displayed in a monospace font.

questions.question: What is the <pre> element?
questions.answer: The <pre> element represents preformatted text. It preserves whitespace and line breaks.

questions.question: What is the <blockquote> element?
questions.answer: The <blockquote> element represents a long quotation. It's typically indented and may include a cite attribute.

questions.question: What is the <cite> element?
questions.answer: The <cite> element represents the title of a work. It's used to cite sources and references.

questions.question: What is the <q> element?
questions.answer: The <q> element represents a short inline quotation. Browsers typically add quotation marks automatically.

questions.question: What is the <abbr> element?
questions.answer: The <abbr> element represents an abbreviation. The title attribute provides the full form.

questions.question: What is the <address> element?
questions.answer: The <address> element represents contact information. It's typically used for author or organization contact details.

questions.question: What is the <del> element?
questions.answer: The <del> element represents deleted text. It's typically displayed with a strikethrough.

questions.question: What is the <ins> element?
questions.answer: The <ins> element represents inserted text. It's typically displayed with an underline.

questions.question: What is the <sub> element?
questions.answer: The <sub> element represents subscript text. It's typically displayed below the baseline.

questions.question: What is the <sup> element?
questions.answer: The <sup> element represents superscript text. It's typically displayed above the baseline.

questions.question: What is the <hr> element?
questions.answer: The <hr> element represents a thematic break. It's typically displayed as a horizontal line.

questions.question: What is the <wbr> element?
questions.answer: The <wbr> element represents a word break opportunity. It suggests where text can break to the next line.

questions.question: What is the <div> element?
questions.answer: The <div> element is a generic container for grouping content. It has no semantic meaning and is used for styling and layout.

questions.question: What is the <span> element?
questions.answer: The <span> element is an inline container for grouping content. It has no semantic meaning and is used for styling.

questions.question: What is the <h1> to <h6> elements?
questions.answer: Heading elements represent different levels of headings. <h1> is the most important, <h6> is the least important.

questions.question: What is the <ul> element?
questions.answer: The <ul> element represents an unordered list. It contains <li> elements.

questions.question: What is the <ol> element?
questions.answer: The <ol> element represents an ordered list. It contains <li> elements numbered sequentially.

questions.question: What is the <li> element?
questions.answer: The <li> element represents a list item. It's used in <ul> and <ol> elements.

questions.question: What is the <dl> element?
questions.answer: The <dl> element represents a description list. It contains <dt> and <dd> elements.

questions.question: What is the <dt> element?
questions.answer: The <dt> element represents a term in a description list. It's paired with <dd> for the definition.

questions.question: What is the <dd> element?
questions.answer: The <dd> element represents a definition in a description list. It provides the definition for a <dt>.

questions.question: What is the <form> element?
questions.answer: The <form> element represents a form for user input. It contains form controls like inputs and buttons.

questions.question: What is the <input> element?
questions.answer: The <input> element represents an input field. The type attribute determines the input type.

questions.question: What is the <textarea> element?
questions.answer: The <textarea> element represents a multi-line text input. It's useful for longer text entries.

questions.question: What is the <select> element?
questions.answer: The <select> element represents a dropdown list. It contains <option> elements.

questions.question: What is the <option> element?
questions.answer: The <option> element represents an option in a <select> element. It can be selected by the user.

questions.question: What is the <optgroup> element?
questions.answer: The <optgroup> element groups related options in a <select> element. It helps organize long lists.

questions.question: What is the <button> element?
questions.answer: The <button> element represents a clickable button. It can submit forms or trigger JavaScript.

questions.question: What is the <fieldset> element?
questions.answer: The <fieldset> element groups related form controls. It's often used with <legend> for accessibility.

questions.question: What is the <legend> element?
questions.answer: The <legend> element provides a caption for a <fieldset> element. It improves form accessibility.

questions.question: What is the <datalist> element?
questions.answer: The <datalist> element provides predefined options for an input. It works with the list attribute.

questions.question: What is the <output> element?
questions.answer: The <output> element represents the result of a calculation. It's useful for displaying computed values.

questions.question: What is the <progress> element?
questions.answer: The <progress> element represents progress of a task. It displays a progress bar.

questions.question: What is the <meter> element?
questions.answer: The <meter> element represents a scalar measurement. It displays a gauge or measurement indicator.

questions.question: What is the <a> element?
questions.answer: The <a> element represents a hyperlink. The href attribute specifies the link destination.

questions.question: What is the element?
questions.answer: The element represents an image. The src attribute specifies the image URL.

questions.question: What is the <picture> element?
questions.answer: The <picture> element provides multiple image sources. It allows responsive images based on device capabilities.

questions.question: What is the <source> element?
questions.answer: The <source> element specifies media sources for <picture>, <audio>, and <video> elements.

questions.question: What is the <audio> element?
questions.answer: The <audio> element embeds audio content. It supports multiple formats and provides playback controls.

questions.question: What is the <video> element?
questions.answer: The <video> element embeds video content. It supports multiple formats and provides playback controls.

questions.question: What is the <track> element?
questions.answer: The <track> element specifies text tracks for <video> elements. It's used for subtitles and captions.

questions.question: What is the <iframe> element?
questions.answer: The <iframe> element embeds another HTML page. It's useful for embedding external content.

questions.question: What is the <embed> element?
questions.answer: The <embed> element embeds external content like plugins. It's less commonly used than <iframe>.

questions.question: What is the <object> element?
questions.answer: The <object> element embeds external resources. It's used for plugins and other embedded content.

questions.question: What is the <canvas> element?
questions.answer: The <canvas> element provides a drawing surface for graphics. It requires JavaScript for drawing.

questions.question: What is the <svg> element?
questions.answer: The <svg> element represents scalable vector graphics. It allows drawing shapes and paths.

questions.question: What is the <table> element?
questions.answer: The <table> element represents tabular data. It contains <tr>, <td>, and other table elements.

questions.question: What is the <tr> element?
questions.answer: The <tr> element represents a table row. It contains <td> or <th> elements.

questions.question: What is the <td> element?
questions.answer: The <td> element represents a table data cell. It contains the actual table data.

questions.question: What is the <th> element?
questions.answer: The <th> element represents a table header cell. It's typically bold and centered.

questions.question: What is the <thead> element?
questions.answer: The <thead> element groups header rows in a table. It improves table structure and accessibility.

questions.question: What is the <tbody> element?
questions.answer: The <tbody> element groups body rows in a table. It improves table structure and accessibility.

questions.question: What is the <tfoot> element?
questions.answer: The <tfoot> element groups footer rows in a table. It improves table structure and accessibility.

questions.question: What is the <caption> element?
questions.answer: The <caption> element provides a title for a table. It's displayed above or below the table.

questions.question: What is the <colgroup> element?
questions.answer: The <colgroup> element groups columns in a table. It allows styling multiple columns.

questions.question: What is the <col> element?
questions.answer: The <col> element specifies column properties in a table. It's used within <colgroup>.

questions.question: What is the <style> element?
questions.answer: The <style> element contains CSS styles. It's typically placed in the <head> element.

questions.question: What is the <link> element?
questions.answer: The <link> element links external resources like stylesheets. The rel attribute specifies the relationship.

questions.question: What is the <script> element?
questions.answer: The <script> element contains JavaScript code. It can be inline or link to external files.

questions.question: What is the <noscript> element?
questions.answer: The <noscript> element provides content for users with JavaScript disabled. It's displayed when JavaScript is not available.

questions.question: What is the <template> element?
questions.answer: The <template> element holds HTML that's not rendered. It's useful for JavaScript templating.

questions.question: What is the <details> element?
questions.answer: The <details> element creates a disclosure widget. It can be expanded or collapsed to show/hide content.

questions.question: What is the <summary> element?
questions.answer: The <summary> element provides a summary for a <details> element. It's the clickable heading.

questions.question: What is the <dialog> element?
questions.answer: The <dialog> element represents a dialog box. It can be modal or modeless.

questions.question: What is the <menu> element?
questions.answer: The <menu> element represents a list of commands. It's used for context menus and toolbars.

questions.question: What is the <menuitem> element?
questions.answer: The <menuitem> element represents a command in a <menu> element. It's rarely used in modern HTML.

questions.question: What is the <data> element?
questions.answer: The <data> element associates content with a machine-readable value. The value attribute specifies the machine-readable value.

questions.question: What is the <bdi> element?
questions.answer: The <bdi> element represents bidirectional text isolation. It's useful for mixed text directions.

questions.question: What is the <bdo> element?
questions.answer: The <bdo> element overrides text direction. The dir attribute specifies the direction.

questions.question: What is the <rp> element?
questions.answer: The <rp> element provides fallback parentheses for ruby annotations. It's used with <ruby> and <rt>.

questions.question: What is the <rt> element?
questions.answer: The <rt> element provides ruby text annotations. It's used with <ruby> for pronunciation guides.

questions.question: What is the <ruby> element?
questions.answer: The <ruby> element provides ruby annotations. It's used for pronunciation guides in East Asian typography.

questions.question: What is the <var> element?
questions.answer: The <var> element represents a variable. It's typically displayed in italics.

questions.question: What is the <kbd> element?
questions.answer: The <kbd> element represents keyboard input. It's typically displayed in a monospace font.

questions.question: What is the <samp> element?
questions.answer: The <samp> element represents sample output. It's typically displayed in a monospace font.
